verification.note: Read the oral-history subsection 12–13, complete chapter-one section III 27–32, and chapter-two opening 33–34 through the performance heading; notes 24–25 and 69–75 read in public transcription. No scan collation or full-book reading. Distinguishes source forms, competing definitions, communal transmission and feedback from writing. verification.note: Read introduction 1–3; Northwest British Columbia case 11–13; complete concluding section IV 13–17; references 18–20 in government-hosted PDF text. Selected intervening comparative passages encountered, not complete paper. Draft discussion, not adopted Commission policy. Case is her interpretation of the 1991 trial decision while appeal was pending in 1993; subsequent law and underlying testimony not checked. Yukon curriculum project credits unnamed community-selected elders, whose identities are not inferred from her different life-story book.

outcomes.finding: Primary Vansina transmission passages and Cruikshank’s situated discussion of Indigenous narratives support qualified expansions of two existing contributions. Definitions, communal circulation, performance and institutional interpretation remain distinct.
outcomes.research_limit: Vansina 1985: oral-history subsection 12–13, complete section III 27–32, chapter-two opening 33–34 before the performance subsection, and notes 24–25, 69–75 read in public transcription. No scan collation or complete book reading. Earlier 1981 primary chapter was already recorded separately. Cruikshank February 1993 draft: introduction 1–3, Northwest British Columbia case 11–13, complete concluding section IV 13–17, bibliography 18–20 read in government PDF text, plus selected intervening passages. This is a draft discussion paper, not adopted Commission policy; trial discussion records the 1993 position, not subsequent legal outcomes.
